description: A real three-candle gap exists, but it is too small against ATR and the middle candle is not a displacement. Doctrine says it is not stored at all.
labelling_rationale: SLS §5.4 separates the existence of a gap from its registration. A bullish gap exists whenever L[c3] > H[c1] with no tolerance, and here candle 0 highs at 100 while candle 2 lows at 100.5, so a genuine 0.5-wide gap exists. Registration is a second, stricter test: the gap must be at least P.ict.fvg_min = 0.25 x ATR, OR the middle candle must satisfy displacement. True ranges for candles 0..2 are 2, 11 and 12.5, summing to 25.5 over three candles for an ATR of exactly 8.5, so the registration floor is 2.125 and the 0.5 gap falls well short. The displacement escape hatch cannot apply either, because §5.10 requires a 20-candle lookback that a three-candle series does not have, so displacements is 0. §5.4's Validation Rules are explicit about the consequence: 'Sub-filter gaps are not stored at all (noise economy — storing everything and filtering later bloats state and invites parameter abuse downstream).' The correct output is therefore not a stored zone in some suppressed state, but no zone whatsoever: zero detected, zero live, no transitions. This case is the regression armour for the opposite failure to the flat-window one — there the risk was inventing structure from noise, here it is hoarding noise as structure. Candle numbers above are scenario-relative; the 297 declared filler candles (SLS §1.9 warm-up) shift them by 297 in the expected output. The filler's high matches the scenario's first candle so the seam cannot form a swing high, and its low sits below so it cannot form a swing low; neither a bullish nor a bearish three-candle gap spans the seam, so declared history registers no zone of its own. Extended 2026-08-23 when the harness began running the OTE, order-block and interaction passes alongside the FVG pass, in the pipeline's own order. The added counts follow SLS 5.9's grammar table: a Touch is any candle whose range intersects the band; a Rejection is a touch that closes outside on the polarity side with a wick of at least 0.3 x ATR into the zone; a Mitigation is reaching half the zone depth and closing outside on the polarity side; and a Respect is 'Rejection or Mitigation without any close-through', which is why respects track them rather than adding a third event. Dealing ranges and order blocks are zero throughout: 5.7 needs confirmed external swings that these short scenarios never produce, and 5.1's qualification reads S4/S5 evidence that a zone-only dataset does not generate.
